name: Belovode copper smelting
summary: Slag and slag-coated pottery at the Vinča settlement of Belovode show people extracting copper from ore around 5000 BCE, among Europe's early evidence of smelting.
description: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramic sherds document extraction of copper from ore at a Vinča settlement.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

date.label: by c. 4650 BCE
date.basis: The Trench 3 D/Gradac occupation is approximately 5000–4650 BCE; slag and sherds support an inferred local smelting context, not a hard earliest operation date. The horizon and end are approximate.

events.statement: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramics in the dated Belovode occupation imply local extractive smelting by the end of the cited horizon.
events.caveats: Small samples and contextual dating constrain a horizon; no specific first use, furnace form, economic exchange or global priority is established.

evidence.supports: The physical debris comes from a dated settlement sequence and is interpreted as ore smelting.
